title: Halicin: deep learning identifies an antibiotic
summary: A model trained on about 2,500 molecules screened the roughly 6,000 compounds in the Broad Institute’s Drug Repurposing Hub and identified halicin, which killed many resistant bacteria in the lab and cleared A. baumannii infections in mice within 24 hours. Cell-culture and mouse results, not human studies; the mechanism remains preliminary.
ai_technology: Graph neural network for predicting antibacterial activity

evidence.tested: Bactericidal activity against a wide range of pathogens, including M. tuberculosis and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae; halicin treated C. difficile and pan-resistant A. baumannii infections in mice. Of 23 tested predictions from over 107 million ZINC15 molecules, eight were antibacterial.
evidence.unknown: Human safety and efficacy are not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: A deep neural network predicted antibacterial activity across chemical libraries; candidates were then tested experimentally.
